A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PERM, with matching authors, architecture and central equations. All supplied pages are readable. However, v1 repeatedly references a separate supplement absent from its PDF, whereas v4 includes Appendices A–E. This limits comparisons of implementation details and supplementary experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction errors in Tables 1–2, architecture comparisons, and qualitative hair reconstruction, interpolation and generation results.

after.justification: v4 reports original strand and hairstyle reconstruction experiments, alternate-training-data results, ablations, checkpoint comparisons and application demonstrations.

M1.justification: The central frequency-PCA representation, 10/54 coefficient split, StyleGAN2 generator, blending U-Net, residual VAE and Equations 1–6 remain unchanged. v4 specifies differentiable rendering and a penetration loss for reconstruction, but v1 delegates that procedure to its unavailable Supplemental C.5. Their status as procedural changes versus fuller documentation cannot be established.

E1.justification: v4 describes a curl-diverse, 80-hairstyle training corpus and evaluates dynamic, tilted-pose and occluded-image cases. The relationship to v1's 100 artist-groomed evaluation hairstyles and supplementary reconstruction examples is undocumented in the supplied material. Consequently, the extent of genuinely new data or scenario coverage is uncertain; the confirmed test-set-size revision belongs to E3.

E2.justification: The strand comparison expands from v1's positional and frequency VAEs to frequency, CNN, Transformer and ModSIREN MLP VAEs in v4 Table 1, substantially broadening the evaluated neural alternatives. GroomGen and HairStep remain comparators. v4 also reports comparisons against official GroomGen component checkpoints, rather than relying exclusively on its reimplementation.

E3.justification: The stated evaluation collection changes from 17 public plus 100 artist-groomed hairstyles in v1 Section 4 to 17 public hairstyles in v4 Section 4. v4 additionally describes training strand representations on 80 private hairstyles and testing them on those 17 public examples. These materially revise the reported evaluation design; they do not establish that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: The existing guide-synthesis, interpolation and residual-network comparisons are retained, largely in Appendix C. v4 extends the residual ablation with a no-residual-texture control and reports substantial GroomGen diagnostics: official-checkpoint comparisons and a 200-to-100-point strand-resolution test. Appendix B.4 also supplies component-count sensitivity and alternate-training-data robustness analyses, although their complete correspondence to v1's missing supplement cannot be checked.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. Results remain point estimates and qualitative comparisons. v4's explained-variance plots concern PCA data representation, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Reported results change substantially. Frequency-PCA position/curvature errors change from 0.004/0.569 in v1 Table 1 to 0.020/2.150 in v4 Table 1. Full-hair PERM errors change from 0.805/0.179 in v1 Table 2 to 1.658/0.769 in v4 Section 4.2. These accompany a changed stated test set and are not same-setting regressions. v4 also reports additional baseline, alternate-training-data and diagnostic results.

T1.justification: The central mathematical representation and loss definitions in Equations 1–6 are retained. No new theorem, proof or formal guarantee appears. The additional curvature formula and optimization expressions document existing evaluation and fitting procedures; the biological motivation and PCA sensitivity discussion do not constitute new theoretical results.

C1.justification: Both abstracts and introductions claim a frequency-PCA hair representation that separates global structure from local details and serves as a generic prior for reconstruction, editing and image generation. These central contributions remain intact. Reframing interpolation as parameter editing and moving 3D parameterization into evaluation principally change presentation.

C2.justification: v4 expands v1's training-data limitation into a fuller account of failure mechanisms, including inadequate per-pixel supervision, fine-detail reconstruction failures and accessory occlusion in Appendix E. It also explains the proposed generalization role of low-variance PCA components and interprets GroomGen much more critically as unstable and unreliable, while acknowledging incomplete access to its implementation.

D1.justification: v4 supplies network specifications, hardware/software versions, training budgets and optimization schedules in Appendices A–B, and changes the abstract's access pointer from a promised GitHub release to a project page. However, v1 explicitly assigns technical details to its unavailable supplement. The extent of newly disclosed information versus incorporated existing documentation cannot be reliably determined.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially refocused from broad geometric and parametric modeling surveys toward volumetric, strand-based, generative and PCA hair representations. v4 adds biological hair-classification literature and recent Gaussian-based reconstruction work, explicitly positions PERM as the first neural architecture incorporating PCA strand representations, and substantially strengthens its criticism of GroomGen.

P1.justification: The introduction and related-work narrative are extensively rewritten, with more consistent global-structure/local-curl terminology. Experiments and applications become separate sections, 3D parameterization moves into evaluation, existing ablations move to Appendix C, and limitations move to Appendix E alongside a new conclusion. This is substantial reorganization beyond added scientific content.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation and substantially revises its displays. Table 1 gains comparator columns; v1 Table 2 is separated into v4 Table 3 and an inline full-hair comparison. The residual-texture figure becomes a geometry comparison with texture insets and an additional control. New explanatory and diagnostic figures accompany relocation of retained interpolation and ablation figures.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens the empirical argument through broader neural baselines, partial verification against official GroomGen checkpoints, and clearer failure analysis. These provide a limited net improvement in evidential support and transparency. The narrower primary test collection and unavailable official upsampler constrain its stronger GroomGen criticism, while v1's missing supplement prevents attributing all appendix detail to the revision.
